clinician.final_diagnosis: Diffuse Melanosis Cutis (DMC) in the course of metastatic melanoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old man with a history of malignant melanoma presented with a 4-month history of dark gray skin discoloration, general weakness, loss of appetite, weight loss, and dark urine. Initial workup excluded Addison's disease and porphyria. A diagnostic skin biopsy revealed intracellular and extracellular melanin deposition in the dermis, including melanoma metastatic cells (Melan-A (+), HMB45 (+), S100(+), CD68 (−)), confirming diffuse melanosis cutis due to metastatic melanoma. Imaging tests subsequently revealed a 2 cm tumor in the right kidney. The patient refused treatment and died eight months after the appearance of DMC.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with dark gray skin coloration on face, neck, and upper torso, along with systemic symptoms including general weakness, loss of appetite, weight loss, and dark urine.
Patient had a history of malignant melanoma with two prior surgeries and sentinel node metastasis.

Skin biopsy revealed intracellular and extracellular melanin deposition in the dermis, with intracellular deposition in CD68(+) macrophages and melanoma metastatic cells (Melan-A (+), HMB45 (+), S100(+), CD68 (−)).
Imaging tests (abdominal, thyroid and cardiac ultrasonography, chest x-ray and CT, colonoscopy, PET-CT) revealed a 2 cm tumor in the right kidney.
The patient refused treatment and died eight months after DMC appeared.
